transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Olivia (Ceres - Head of MLOps), Marcus (Ceres - VP Product), Priya (Ceres - SRE)

Summary (auto): quick QBR/check-in. Focus on a recent cost spike, a P99 latency regression after the last model rollout, and next steps to start a 4-week stability+cost sprint. Redwood to provide pricing and security artifacts.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today. quick agenda — usage & cost review, reliability incidents, then handoff for the sprint. is that still what you wanted, olivia?
[00:16] Olivia: Yeah that's right. we had some spikes the last two weeks after the new feature ship, figured we'd go through the numbers and figure out if this is redwood config or on our side.
[00:25] Marcus: And to be frank we also want a clear path to dedicated capacity if the pilot shows good econ. pricing was ... okay but we need lower tail latency and predictable p99.
[00:36] Diego: totally. quick housekeeping, i'll call out where i think latency/cost tradeoffs are and possible knobs — batching, kv cache scope, quantization, routing to smaller model variants.
[00:48] Priya: For us the big question: can we run in our VPC with customer-managed KMS? compliance team wants predictable audit logs, SSO, RBAC. also who owns the KV cache if we do private deploy?
[01:05] Sophie: Yes — private deployment supports VPC and KMS integrations, and we can give an audit log export. Diego i'll let you add specifics on KMS and cache ownership.
[01:15] Diego: Sure. so for private we support customer-managed KMS via standard cloud KMS providers, and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. as for KV cache, if you run Redwood Private on your VPC the cache can be colocated and you retain control. with hosted dedicated we provide cache but we can enable prefix caching policies.
[01:38] Olivia: when you say "prefix caching" is that the automatic reuse across sessions? i've seen weird cache eviction issues previously.
[01:45] Diego: yeah — automatic prefix and kv caching, but eviction policies depend on memory and sequence length distribution. if your prompts have long tails it can evict more frequently — that's likely what caused p99 to spike after the feature with longer contexts.
[02:02] Marcus: can you explain how that resulted in cost going up? i expected caching to lower token costs.
[02:08] Diego: caching helps but the feature increased average sequence length by ~40%, so more tokens per request. also continuous batching increased throughput but not enough for p99 because tail latency is dominated by those long sequences hitting cold kv states. so tokens burned up and average cost per user rose.
[02:28] Priya: okay that tracks. is there a quick mitigation? like reduce context length or force fallbacks to a smaller variant for long sequences?
[02:36] Sophie: we've seen two pragmatic paths — immediate: set a policy to route >1024 tokens to a cheaper/fast variant and adjust batching window; medium: pilot dedicated capacity with tuned compile kernels and larger KV memory to reduce evictions.
[02:52] Olivia: sounds reasonable. what's the impact to latency if we route to smaller variant for those long calls?
[02:58] Diego: typically you trade some quality for latency/cost. For many of your calls (the ones that are more heuristics/regex-like), the smaller variant's outputs are fine; for high-quality text generation we keep the primary model. we can do A/B to measure quality delta.
[03:16] Marcus: and pricing wise, we need an estimate for reserved capacity and a pilot credit. last time the committed plan quote we saw was kind of opaque.
[03:25] Sophie: understood. i'll put together a transparent worksheet that shows token unit costs, reserved hour rates, and expected break-even at your current traffic shape. will include pilot credit tiers.
[03:35] Olivia: great. also, can we get more details on SLAs? your console shows per-route metrics but our execs want a P99 SLA number.
[03:44] Sophie: our Dedicated offering comes with SLA-backed latency targets; for hosted we publish performance profiles but SLA is for dedicated/reserved. we'll attach the SLA excerpt.
[03:55] Priya: one security question — do you support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning? and iso/ SOC2?
[04:02] Diego: yes to SAML/SCIM, and Redwood is SOC2 Type II. we'll attach a controls matrix and SOC2 attestation in the security pack.
[04:12] Olivia: nice. those docs are key for our procurement folks.
[04:17] Marcus: i want to dig into the P99 regression — can Diego run a benchmark that simulates our traffic shape? we can share a sample prompt set.
[04:24] Diego: absolutely. please share the prompt set and traffic distribution and i'll run a 1k concurrent req benchmark, measure p50/p95/p99 and token costs.
[04:33] Sophie: timeline? when can you share the prompt set?
[04:36] Olivia: we'll send the set by Friday. internal review needed but should be done.
[04:40] Sophie: perfect. Diego you'll run the benchmark and share results next week.
[04:45] Diego: will do. i'll also try a config where long sequences are routed to a smaller model so we can measure tradeoffs.
[04:52] Priya: about pilot infra, if we do dedicated we need to know autoscaling behavior; last time there was a spike and scale-up lagged. how do you handle burst?
[05:03] Diego: Dedicated pools support configurable autoscaling and burst capacity; you can set min/max and an emergency burst that draws from a shared burst pool. i'll share the autoscale docs + recommended settings for your traffic shape.
[05:15] Sophie: and we can enable graceful fallback policies — e.g., if the dedicated pool saturates route to a compatible hosted variant with reduced SLOs, so service stays online.
[05:25] Marcus: that's good — operationally acceptable. question on observability: can we get token-level breakdowns by route and model version?
[05:33] Diego: yes, the console shows per-route cost and latency; we'll give you a dashboard template and tracing hooks you can add to your backend.
[05:42] Olivia: on the timeline, our execs want a 4-week pilot starting mid-November if the numbers line up. what's the earliest you can provision dedicated pool and run the pilot?
[05:52] Sophie: technically we can stand up a pilot pool within 7-10 business days after contract/commit. for VPC/private on-prem it's longer; for dedicated hosted it is faster. propose we aim to kick off week of 11/16 pending agreement.
[06:05] Priya: can the pilot be in our VPC? that's non-negotiable for security-sensitive traffic.
[06:11] Diego: yes for Redwood Private we can deploy in a customer VPC. we'll need network details and KMS configuration to estimate lead time.
[06:20] Marcus: a procurement question — do you have a fixed pilot SOW or is it ad-hoc? we prefer a short SOW with acceptance criteria.
[06:27] Sophie: we have a pilot SOW template; i'll attach it. typical acceptance criteria: p99 latency target, decrease in avg cost per active session by X%, and stability in error rates below Y% over 2 weeks. you define the X/Y and we'll align.
[06:40] Olivia: we'll propose the SLO numbers and get back.
[06:43] Sophie: great. a couple of specific follow-ups — priya you mentioned SOC2, we'll attach the attestation; marcus you'll confirm success criteria; olivia send prompt set.
[06:52] Marcus: yep, will do.
[06:53] Priya: small note — can we get the log retention options? our compliance likes 1 year export in raw logs.
[06:59] Diego: yes retention is configurable; we support log forwarding to your storage for long-term retention.
[07:05] Olivia: any blockers from your side?
[07:07] Sophie: none immediate. we just need the prompt set and procurement to confirm timeline. we'll follow up with the pricing worksheet and attach security pack.
[07:16] Marcus: sounds good.
[07:18] Sophie: ok final recap: 1) Redwood to send reserved pricing worksheet + pilot credit by 11/06. 2) Diego to run benchmarks after receiving prompt set and share results by 11/10. 3) Customer to send prompt set and confirm pilot success criteria by 11/09. 4) Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 11/16.
[07:37] Olivia: thanks everyone.
[07:38] Sophie: thank you all. we'll update the CRM ticket with attachments.
[07:40] (meeting ends)

Notes: some transcription errors likely; product names sometimes transcribed as "private deploy" vs "Redwood Private". Links referenced: security pack (will be attached in CRM), pilot SOW template (link: https://redwood.example/sow-template), reserved-pricing worksheet (attached).
